text:
Jim stood in the back of the studio, his neck craning so far forward he could see the instructor’s left earlobe from the ceiling tiles. He had intended to join the "Gentle Stretching for Beginners" class, but a misread flyer and a profound misunderstanding of the word "Advanced" had landed him in "Power Vinyasa Flow: The Ascension."

The instructor, a woman named Serenity who looked like she was made entirely of willow branches and judgment, clapped her hands. "Alright, everyone. Let’s find our center. Inhale, and reach for the sky."

Jim reached. He reached so hard he pulled his own shoulder out of its socket, but he kept his face neutral, hoping no one noticed. He was trying to mimic the woman in front of him, who was currently balancing on one leg while humming a low B-flat.

"Exhale," Serenity commanded. "Fold forward. Let gravity do the work."

Jim folded. He folded with the enthusiasm of a man trying to hide a bad smell. As he bent, his tight yoga pants, purchased specifically for this occasion because he thought they would help with "alignment," began to sing. It wasn't a metaphorical song. It was a high-pitched, rubbery squeak that echoed off the mirrored walls.

Serenity paused. "Is someone playing a theremin?"

Jim froze. He tried to stand up slowly, but his body had other plans. As he straightened, a sound erupted from his posterior that was less of a 'toot' and more of a tuba solo played by a disgruntled goose.

The class didn't break. They didn't laugh. They did something worse. They stared. The woman in front of him, still humming the B-flat, stopped humming. The man to his left, holding a perfect headstand, began to sweat profusely.

Jim, panicked, tried to cover his face with his hands. In doing so, he lost his balance. He stumbled forward, his long arms flailing like a giraffe trying to catch a falling leaf. He tripped over his own mat, which had curled up at the corners.

As he fell, he let out a grunt that sounded suspiciously like a deflating balloon. He hit the floor with a thud that shook the water bottles on the shelf.

Silence.

Serenity walked over, her bare feet silent on the wood.
